These Bail Applications are filed under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.

sentences.text: The petitioner in these cases is the same person.
2. Petitioner is the accused in Crime Nos.1008, 1009 & 1010 of 2024 of Palarivattom Police Station.

The above case is registered against the petitioner and another alleging offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 r/w 34 IPC.
3.

The prosecution case in brief is that, promising work permit to Canada, the petitioner and the 1 st accused collected huge amount from the defacto complainants in these cases and the work visa was not provided and the amount was B.A.Nos.10441, 10448 & 10455 of 2024 2025:KER:1617 also not returned.
Hence it is alleged that the accused committed the above said offence.

4. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
5.
Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is the wife of the 1st accused and she has no connection with the business of the 1 st accused.
The counsel submitted that the petitioner is ready to abide any conditions if this Court grant her bail.
6. The Public Prosecutor opposed these bail applications and submitted that huge amount was collected by the accused in these cases and cheated the defacto complainants in these cases.
7. This Court considered the contentions of the petitioner and the Public Prosecutor.
It is true that the allegations against the petitioner are serious.
But the main allegation is against the 1st accused.
Petitioner is the wife of the 1 st accused.

According to the counsel for the petitioner, the petitioner is now residing at Thiruvananthapuram and she has no connection with B.A.Nos.10441, 10448 &
10455 of 2024 2025:KER:1617 the business of the 1st accused.
I do not want to make any observation about the same.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I think the petitioner can be released on bail after imposing stringent conditions.
But I make it clear that this order is not applicable to the 1 st accused and the bail application of the 1st accused will be considered separately in accordance with law.
8. Moreover, it is a well accepted principle that the bail is the rule and the jail is the exception.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Chidambaram.

P v Directorate of Enforcement [2019 (16) SCALE 870],
after considering all the earlier judgments, observed that, the basic jurisprudence relating to bail remains the same inasmuch as the grant of bail is the rule and refusal is the exception so as to ensure that the accused has the opportunity of securing fair trial.

entities.text: P v Directorate of Enforcement [2019 (16) SCALE 870]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. Recently the Apex Court in Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
considered the point in detail.

entities.text: Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relevant paragraph of the above judgment is extracted hereunder.
We may note that personal liberty is an important aspect of our constitutional mandate.

The occasion to arrest an accused during investigation arises when custodial investigation becomes necessary or it is a heinous crime or where there is a possibility of influencing the witnesses or accused may abscond.
Merely because an arrest can be made because it is lawful does not mandate that arrest must be made.

A distinction Sruthy Thilak vs State Of Kerala on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109604101/
4 must be made between the existence of the power to arrest and the justification for exercise of it.

entities.text: Sruthy Thilak vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

(Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189:
(1994) 4 SCC 260: 1994 (1) KLT 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981)) If arrest is made routine, it can cause incalculable harm to the reputation and self-esteem of a person.

entities.text:
Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189:
(1994) 4 SCC 260: 1994 (1) KLT 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981)

sentences.text: If the Investigating Officer has no reason to believe that the accused will abscond or disobey summons and has, in fact, throughout cooperated with the investigation we fail to appreciate why there should be a compulsion on the officer to arrest the accused."

10. In Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2023 KHC 6961], the Apex Court observed that even if the allegation is one of grave economic offence, it is not a rule that bail should be denied in every case.

sentences.text:
11. Considering the dictum laid down in the above decision and considering the facts and circumstances of these B.A.Nos.10441, 10448 & 10455 of 2024 2025:KER:1617 cases, these Bail Applications are allowed with the following directions:
1. The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within two weeks from today and shall undergo interrogation.
2.

After interrogation, if the Investigating Officer propose to arrest the petitioner, she shall be released on bail on executing a bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the arresting officer concerned.
3. The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer for interrogation as and when required.
The petitioner shall co-

operate with the investigation and shall not, directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade her from B.A.Nos.10441, 10448 & 10455 of 2024 2025:KER:1617 disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
4. Petitioner shall not leave India without permission of the jurisdictional Court.

5. Petitioner shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which she is accused, or suspected,
of the commission of which she is suspected.

6. Needless to mention, it would be well within the powers of the investigating officer to investigate the matter and, if necessary, to effect recoveries on the information, if any, given by the petitioner even while the petitioner is on bail as laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi) and another [2020 (1) KHC 663].
